question: What small condition did Stoics attach to every plan, so that failure could not wound them?
answer: If nothing prevents it. Seneca says the wise man undertakes everything with a reservation: I will sail, unless something stops me; I will become praetor, unless something stands in the way. What he staked was the effort, never the result. A storm that cancels the voyage cancels nothing the Stoic had promised himself.
move: Promise the effort in full and the outcome only on conditions.
ask: What have I promised unconditionally that I should have promised only as effort?
reference: Seneca, On Benefits 4.34, trans. Griffin & Inwood, University of Chicago Press, 2011; On Tranquillity of Mind 13, in Dialogues and Essays, trans. Davie, Oxford University Press, 2007
